subject: problem setting MKL to use more than 4 cores

messages.author: 78b4516dd8135186
messages.subject: problem setting MKL to use more than 4 cores
parts:
I recently upgraded to RRO 3.3.2, and installed MKL.  My computer is a Zareason Limbo 6250a (with 8-core AMD processor), running Ubuntu 12.04 LTS.

I would like to set MKL to use 7 cores for parallel processing, but it is requiring a maximum of 4 cores. See some relevant R commands and results below:

> detectCores()
[1] 8
> getMKLthreads()
[1] 4
> setMKLthreads(7)

Number of threads at maximum: no change has been made.

Is there a good reason I cannot use more than 4 cores with MKL, or a way to do so?

Thanks for any suggestions.
Jason

messages.author: 149440eddb848db9
messages.subject: Re: problem setting MKL to use more than 4 cores
parts:
Hi, Jason

At a guess, you are using a 4-core machine with hyperthreading.

The Intel MKL only works on real cores, not the hyperthreading, so the maximum in your case would be 4 cores.

Hyperthreading means that the same physical core acts to run 2 processes at the same time Thus, for high performance computing, you can not get any additional benefit from the hyperthreading.

I hope this helps.

Andrie

I've experienced a similar issue that never bothered me enough to research. I have a triple booted MacBook Pro. On OSX, RRO uses 4 cores --- but on Windows it only uses 2.

What do you make of that? I mean I've always known (and noticed) that Windows runs R absurdly slower than OSX, and that Windows has a lot more difficulty using parallel processing even when coerced manually. So I guess I always attributed the 2/4 core difference to something related to that headache. But your response is making me wonder how many cores I actually have, because either Windows or OSX is lying to me ;)

messages.author: 67f7081cbd450705
messages.subject: Re: problem setting MKL to use more than 4 cores
parts:
I have an 8 core AMD processor too, an FX9590. I used the MKL on my windows machine and it ran on all 8 cores. 

I will say that the MKL on an Intel processor with 4 cores is MUCH MUCH faster than my AMD processor using all 8 cores.
Intel says that you can "force" the MKL to use all your cores by making a change in the system environment variable. I believe you set Number_of_processors = 8.  They also warn that the MKL uses the number of cores it feels it needs to use and forcing it to use more cores can slow down the calcs.

messages.author: 9ca0345d553844f2
messages.subject: Re: problem setting MKL to use more than 4 cores
parts:
Hi Jacob,

On OS X, RRO may be reporting the number of physical plus the number of virtual cores. In your case, that might be a total of 4 cores.  This can be confirmed by looking at the number of physical cores reported in the System Information report.

Regards,

Josée Martens
Revolution Analytics, a Microsoft company

messages.author: 9ca0345d553844f2
messages.subject: Re: problem setting MKL to use more than 4 cores
parts:
Hi Jason,

Perhaps this will answer your question.  We found the following on a Mathematica Google Group site:

 

The end result is that a Bulldozer core is "worth" about half a Sandy   

Bridge core, clock for clock, especially in floating-point workloads since   

a single FP unit is shared between two of what AMD calls cores (indeed,   

many have said that AMD's "8 core" processors are more correctly referred   

to as genuinely having 4 cores due to much shared apparatus, but for   

marketing reasons, AMD is obviously not buying that argument).

 

Since MKL is all about floating point computations, if there are only 4 FP units, it is possible that MKL is seeing 4 cores where AMD is claiming 8…
